title: Opportunistic eviction and shadow-admission lanes prototype for progressive response thinning
creator: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Summary:
We need a low-risk, evaluative prototype that explores a hybrid load-shedding approach combining (1) opportunistic eviction of non-critical KV cache entries and queued requests, (2) a set of shadow (observability-only) admission lanes to validate admission heuristics without impacting real traffic, and (3) progressive response thinning (graceful thinning of outputs) when falling back to lower-fidelity model variants or truncated responses. The goal is to reduce tail-cost spikes and preserve latency SLOs for critical tenants during multi-region overloads and during circuit-breaker activations.

Motivation & context:
- Recent incidents showed P99 latency spikes when regional capacity was saturated and cascading retries amplified load. Existing strategies (hard token trimming and blunt circuit breakers) can be too aggressive for some customers and cause unacceptable functional regressions.
- We want an operator-friendly path to design and tune softer degradation modes that are measurable before they hit prod.

Proposal (high level):
1) Opportunistic eviction: implement a small per-shard opctx that can evict low-value KV cache entries and drop low-priority queued tasks before admission. Eviction uses a composite score (last-access, tenant-priority, estimated cost-to-serve).
2) Shadow admission lanes: create a parallel admission decision pipeline that mirrors incoming requests and runs new heuristics (probabilistic admission, predicted latency model). Shadow lanes log decision outcomes and suggested actions but do not change live routing. This lets us calibrate acceptance thresholds without customer impact.
3) Progressive response thinning: implement a middleware that can trim generation outputs in controlled stages (suffix-trim, N-token budget reduction, lower-sampling temperature) applied after model fallback selection. Each stage has tracked fidelity impact metrics.
4) Operator tooling: console view showing shadow-lane suggestions vs actual rejections, expected SLO impact, and a quick toggle to flip a heuristic from shadow to active for a controlled subset of traffic (canary by tenant or region).

Metrics to instrument:
- Shadow suggestion acceptance rate and precision (how often a shadow-suggested reject would have prevented a P99 violation).
- Delta in P50/P95/P99 latencies after enabling opportunistic eviction.
- Functional regression signals: metrics derived from prompt-set evals (BLEU/ROUGE-like heuristics) for representative prompts.
- Cost delta (tokens served, GPU seconds) after applying progressive thinning.

Compatibility & boundaries:
- Must work across hosted and Dedicated modes; in Private deployments the eviction must be controllable by customer policy (default off).
- Should not require model changes; all thinning operates at RT response layer or by selecting compatible lower-fidelity model variants already in the catalog.

Delivery plan (spikes + prototype):
Week 1: design spike, implement shadow-lane stub and telemetry schema.
Week 2: implement opportunistic eviction module and local simulation harness.
Week 3: progressive thinning module + end-to-end in staging; run controlled replay experiments.
Week 4: dashboard + canary toggle; prepare rollout playbook and runbook.

Why this is different from previous work:
- Unlike our existing banded-shedding work, this prototype emphasizes a shadow-first approach so we can measure false-positive/negative rates before any live rejections.
- Opportunistic eviction targets cache and queued work, not just immediate request trimming, giving us an earlier chance to reduce load without visible functional changes.

Open questions:
- How to signal tenant-level priorities (we have token-bucket weights today, but need a compact priority score for eviction).
- Risk of under-estimating fidelity loss from progressive thinning; need a small evaluation harness to measure user-facing quality impact.

Referenced artifacts: design doc (draft) https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RUN/pages/Load+Shedding+V2, replay harness proto PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7890
acceptance_criteria: Shadow lanes ingest 100% of staging traffic and emit decision logs (no live rejections)
Eviction module can safely reclaim cache/queue capacity and reduce P99 tail by at least 10% in synthetic overload replay
Progressive thinning implements at least three configurable stages and exposes fidelity metrics for each
Console shows side-by-side shadow suggestion vs actual admission for a selected tenant/region
Operator can flip a heuristic to active for a bounded canary without service downtime
tasks: Spike: telemetry schema and shadow-lane contract (Aisha)
Build opportunistic eviction engine and scoring function (SWE pair)
Create staging replay and run experiments (SRE)
Draft runbook and rollback steps (Oncall + PM)
comments: 2026-03-02 Aisha Kapoor: Kickoff meeting notes attached in design doc. Agreed to shadow-first approach to avoid customer regressions.
2026-03-04 Miguel Torres: PR opened for shadow-lane skeleton - https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7890. Needs telemetry naming review (cc @Jordan Lee).
2026-03-06 Jordan Lee: Reviewed eviction scoring draft, suggested adding a 'cost-to-serve' estimate derived from model seq-length distribution; also flagged potential cold-start eviction headaches.
2026-03-08 Priya Menon (PM): Asked for canary gating by tenant and region; requested default conservative thresholds for Dedicated customers.

2026-03-10 Miguel Torres: Staging replay run #1 completed; observed 12% improvement in P99 under synthetic spike when opportunistic eviction is simulated. Results in /dashboards/load-shedding-v2 (internal link).
decisions: Shadow-first rollout: all heuristics must live in shadow for at least 1 week of replayed/staging traffic before being enabled live.
Eviction scoring will combine last-access (LRU-ish), tenant-priority, and an estimated cost-to-serve; weights initially 0.5/0.3/0.2 respectively.
Progressive thinning will be model-agnostic and configurable per model family; initial stages: suffix-trim, token-budget, lower-sampling-temp.
Canary gating limits: at most 2% of global traffic or a single region at a time for first live enablement.
risks_mitigation: Risk: over-eager eviction causes higher cache misses and increased cost. Mitigation: conservative default weights and TTL bump for recently-evicted items.
Risk: progressive thinning causes unacceptable quality regressions. Mitigation: tie to prompt-set evals and require automated regression checks before enabling.
Risk: shadow telemetry volume costs. Mitigation: sample 10% of requests when traffic > threshold and retain summary aggregates only.
observability: SLO dashboards: compare P99 before/after heuristic enablement with request cohorts
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids changing core admission logic until shadow telemetry shows high precision/recall for suggested rejections.
For Private deployments we will expose a config flag (redwood.private.opportunistic_eviction.enabled) defaulting to false.
Follow-up tickets will include automated threshold tuning and tenant-level policy UI pieces.
